# Legacy payments weren’t built for the world fintech operates in today. | Chermaine Hu · LinkedIn · 2026-03-05

**Chermaine Hu**: Co-Founder & CFO at Episode Six for 11 years 6 months with 11 years 6 months of total professional experience. Based in Austin, Texas, United States [US].

---

Legacy payments weren’t built for the world fintech operates in today.

When we started [Episode Six](https://linkedin.com/company/episode-six), the goal was simple: give banks and fintechs the infrastructure they need to launch and scale without being constrained by legacy systems.

I recently joined @Venture:F to talk about what building modern issuer processing actually looks like — and what we have learned expanding [Episode Six](https://linkedin.com/company/episode-six) across markets like Japan, Australia, Singapore, Hong Kong and the UK.

We also discussed why Austin’s fintech ecosystem continues to grow — and the momentum for women shaping this industry.

If you are building in fintech, payments, or embedded finance, I hope you find the conversation useful.

# Episode Six raises $48M to streamline payment processes

 Kyle Wiggers 

11:25 AM PDT · May 23, 2023

Austin, Texas–based Episode Six, a payments and banking infrastructure provider, today announced that it raised $48 million in a Series C funding round led by Avenir with participation from Anthos Capital. In an email, CEO John Mitchell said that the tranche will be used to expand Episode Six’s go-to-market efforts and scale its business as the company looks to drive digital transformation journeys for banks and companies operating within the payments space.

Episode Six was founded in 2015 by Mitchell, Chermaine Hu and Futeh Kao. Seeking to overcome the limitations of legacy payments tech, the co-founders built a platform designed to streamline various payment processes while reducing costs.

“For CTOs and heads of product who want to grow their books and create competitive products, our platform allows them to launch new products quickly to meet a customer’s evolving needs and capture market share,” Mitchell told TechCrunch in an email interview. “For CIOs looking for payments at scale with safety, security, reliability and cost effectiveness, the platform delivers bank-grade payments’ infrastructure built by industry experts.”

New program allows New Zealanders to grow wealth with every transaction

Wellington, November 20, 2025 – Episode Six, a leading global technology provider of enterprise-grade card issuing and ledger infrastructure, today announced its partnership with leading wealth app Sharesies, to support its newly released debit card. The debit card is the first of its kind in New Zealand to allow customers to earn investments on their spending.

Episode Six’s modern card issuing and ledger technology will power Sharesies’ new debit card offering, enabling multi-currency support, virtual account provisioning, and integrated foreign exchange capabilities. This infrastructure allows Sharesies’ customers to move seamlessly between spending and investing within a single platform.

"Customer experience is at the heart of everything we do. It’s fantastic to partner with a company that truly understands this and offers a solution that perfectly supports our goal. With our debit card, we want our customers to feel confident and in control of their spending while actively supporting their financial future,” says General Manager of Sharesies Personal, Scott Nixon.

# FIS and Episode Six Launch the FIS International Issuing Hub to Power the Next Era of Payments

Back To All Posts

June 3, 2025

Follow us on Facebook

Follow us on LinkedIn

FIS and Episode Six took the stage at Money20/20 to announce their partnership to launch the FIS International Issuing Hub

London, June 03, 2025 – Today at Money20/20, FIS and Episode Six announced a major step forward for the financial services industry: the launch of the FIS International Issuing Hub — a fully cloud-native ecosystem designed to help banks and issuers modernize their payments infrastructure and bring innovative products to market, fast.

This new solution brings together FIS’s global scale and trusted technology with Episode Six’s flexible, future-ready issuer processing capabilities. The result? An ecosystem that meets financial institutions where they are — and equips them to grow, evolve, and lead in an increasingly digital world.

“We’re excited to partner with FIS to deliver a solution that brings unmatched scalability and flexibility to the market,” said John Mitchell, CEO and Co-Founder of Episode Six. “FIS International Issuing Hub sets a new standard in payments, empowering companies to thrive in a rapidly evolving digital economy. FIS International Issuing Hub gives our clients the power to scale, innovate, and excel.”

cards.snippet:
Share this page



In 2026, Chief Financial Officers (CFOs) are navigating a rapidly evolving business landscape shaped by digital transformation, economic uncertainty, and the accelerating adoption of AI and automation. As one CFO community member shared, “We have to strike the right balance between the advancement of AI technology, focusing on the talent pool, having a collaborative mindset, creative thinking, and problem-solving – and these are all shifting.” [...] Across the enterprise, CFOs are aligning closely with their C-suite peers on priorities such as operational excellence, cost management, and innovation. Their ability to anticipate trends, respond to disruption, and lead with vision and agility will be critical to organizational success in the years ahead. [...] Capacity constraints are a major barrier, with 61% of CFO survey respondents citing competing priorities as their most significant challenge. Many finance leaders are responding by investing in talent transformation, including upskilling existing teams, attracting tech-savvy professionals, and building centers of excellence to centralize and automate core processes.
